name: Winning Start: education (Founders Pledge)
summary: Winning Start runs daily remedial literacy and numeracy sessions for primary-school children in South Africa, on the Teaching at the Right Level model. Founders Pledge's 2019 education report estimates its cost-effectiveness through later earnings.

source.title: Education: cause report (2019), Education Cost-Effectiveness Calculation (Public)

sections.title: Into units of value
sections.explainer: charityevals' step: FP's increase in ln(income) per dollar, valued with GiveWell's weight on income.

sections.title: Staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not Founders Pledge's. With credit by share of resources on, staff's pay below what they could earn elsewhere counts as their contribution, and they get their share of the outcome.

rows.label: Effect per beneficiary (SD of test scores)
rows.explainer: Based on the evidence for Teaching at the Right Level: daily one-hour remedial literacy sessions. FP's pessimistic (10th percentile), middle and optimistic (90th) cases.

rows.label: Replicability adjustment
rows.explainer: FP applies none (1 in every case).

rows.label: Cost per beneficiary
rows.explainer: Winning Start's cost per child: $10.92 in FP's middle case, $8 to $12 in its others.

rows.label: Government cost per beneficiary
rows.explainer: In FP's middle case the government expected to invest $2 million in 2018/19, about $50 per child; its pessimistic and optimistic cases put it at 0, so the range runs from 0 to 50. It counts only with credit by share of resources on (FP gives government dollars no value as a cost, row 11).

rows.label: Relative value of government dollars
rows.explainer: How much a dollar of government money spent alongside the charity's counts as a cost: 1 if it would otherwise have been as well spent, 0 if it would otherwise have done no good.

rows.label: Total cost per beneficiary
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources on, the government's money counts in full as a contributor's: its share of the outcome is the share of the cost it paid.

rows.label: Annual salary increase per SD
rows.explainer: The shared figure from FP's 2019 education work: 10%, 1% to 25% across its cases (row 17).

rows.label: Share of the increase that is additional
rows.explainer: The shared figure from FP's 2019 education work: 80%, 50% to 100% across its cases (row 18).

rows.label: Years until the benefit starts
rows.explainer: The shared figure from FP's 2019 education work (row 21).

rows.label: Duration of benefits (years)
rows.explainer: The shared figure from FP's 2019 education work: 5 years, 2 to 20 across its cases (row 22).

rows.label: Discount rate
rows.explainer: The shared discount rate (Your values). FP uses 5% (row 23); the evaluator view pins it there.

rows.label: Present value of ln(income) per SD
rows.explainer: FP's formula: the gain paid at the start of each year for the duration, discounted, then divided by (1 + years until the benefit × rate), simple rather than compound discounting for the wait.

rows.label: Present value of ln(income) per $
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's bottom line for the charity (its Summary tab, balanced case).

rows.label: Cost to double one person's income for a year
rows.explainer: FP multiplies by ln 2: a doubling is ln 2 units of ln(income). Written here with GiveWell's weight on income, 1/ln 2, which is the same number; the evaluator view pins it.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: GiveWell's weight on income turns FP's increase in ln(income) into units of value: one unit is a year of doubled income, so this is one over the cost to double income.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for programs where staff deliver the help themselves (treatment, counselling, coaching, outreach): staff pay is about half the cost. Our judgment; we haven't seen this program's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Health workers and field staff at nonprofits often earn somewhat less than in comparable jobs. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per donor dollar
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
